words.definition: absurdity • feasible • robust • intuition • swift • lack
words.example: Confidentially, I think his suggestion is absurd They are absurdly irrational about the issue.
words.zh: 荒謬•可行•穩健•直覺•迅速•缺乏

words.definition: a share; a part set aside for a special purpose; an assignment of portions
words.example: His allocation of materials was gradually used up.
words.zh: 一份；為特殊目的預留的一部分；部分分配

words.definition: balance that counters an equal element on the other
words.example: He made a balanced presentation of both points of view.
words.zh: 與另一個元素相抗衡的平衡

words.example: The student brazenly defended her thesis.

words.definition: to find or discover, usually by chance or mistake
words.example: While searching the archive, the historian came across a letter that changed the investigation.
words.zh: 發現或發現，通常是偶然或錯誤

words.definition: to finish; to reach a climax or the highest point
words.example: The rock song culminated in a loud guitar solo.
words.zh: 完成；達到高潮或最高點

words.example: The old woman had a pleasant demeanor.

words.definition: to put into use; to put forth an effort
words.example: He had to exert all of his strength to move the heavy box.
Her fallacious argument could not be defended.
It is afeasible design for the high-rise building.
He often relies on his intuition rather than analyzing the situation logically.

words.definition: a need for; an insufficient amount
words.example: There was an inordinate lack of rain last fall.
The dancer has a limber body.
The scholarship gave Leo the financial means to attend university without taking a second job.

words.definition: an opinion formed in advance without experience or knowledge of something
words.example: It is difficult to overcome preconceptions if we are not open to new ideas.
words.zh: 在沒有經驗或知識的情況下預先形成的意見

words.definition: showing good health; in good shape
words.example: The robust economy is expected to continue growing quickly.
words.zh: 表現出身體健康；狀態良好
